claim_summary: With 26 candidate markers and 6 per tube, the classical 130-tube design S(3,6,26) (isomorphic to the inversive plane of order 5) co-measures each of the 2,600 marker triples exactly once.
panel_id: Fig. 1b; Fig. 1c; Fig. 2a; Fig. 2b; Suppl. Fig. 3b
limitation: Marker coordinates are an assigned labelling; backbone channels are counted separately; staining performance is not addressed.

claim_summary: For a fixed candidate set, available parent cells and per-cell capacity, the mean number of directly witnessing cells per triple does not depend on the number of tubes; with equal random tube allocation, balanced coverage gives every target the same expected evidence share.
limitation: An equal evidence share is not an equal interval width and does not mean that every target meets the tolerance.

claim_summary: At the chosen replay tolerances, WINGMEN design nodes at one and two complete rounds reach high half-width attainment and intermediate nodes dip; Levine T recovers correspondingly, but not every parent approaches 100% (e.g. Levine B about 79.3% and 83.7% at 71 and 142 tubes). Splitting a tube's cells into a clone tube with the same panel and pooling the counts leaves every target's evidence unchanged.
panel_id: Fig. 3b; Fig. 3c; Fig. 3d; Suppl. Fig. 2a; Suppl. Fig. 2b
limitation: The e5b replay tolerances are mechanism-display thresholds chosen post hoc; per-donor results are exploratory (grid 180 instead of the specified 195).

claim_summary: Under the uniform threshold offsets examined and at two selected tube nodes, the half-width advantage of the complete-round node over the intermediate node is retained, and the finite-sample reference frequencies of the examined claims remain inside the audit intervals.
limitation: Only uniform offsets (-0.25 to +0.25 asinh units) and two nodes per parent were examined.

claim_summary: Under an artificial 5-slot family constraint, the quadratic orthogonal array covers all 1,250 cross-family triples exactly once with 125 tubes (marker multiplicity 25, pair multiplicity 5); WINGMEN replay half-width attainment is 99.7-100%, against about 91% for this annealing run and about 63% for constrained random.
limitation: The families are artificial and do not model real spillover; results are relative to the baselines used.

claim_summary: Lower-order redundancy of the classical design provides between-tube consistency checks. In the specified joint-relationship-only simulation the combined single + pair check detects 49.0% / 73.5% while single-marker checks detect none; with a fixed test family, blank alarms are 0/1000 and 1/1000 (e5d) and 0/20 (Levine) and 1/20 (WINGMEN) in e5k.
limitation: Common drift and mild composition shifts are essentially undetectable; a pair alarm does not identify which marker failed.

claim_summary: In this 3-design, gating on a candidate marker x leaves the derived 2-design as the usable co-measurement structure: triples of the other 25 markers are covered only 300/2300 (about 13%). Fixing x in the backbone and redesigning restores full conditional triple witnesses; x + 6 needs 7 slots, and with capacity 6 a redesign as x + 5 is required.
limitation: A coverage fraction, not a detection sensitivity; the repair designs are feasible coverings, not proven minima.

claim_summary: In 40 synthetic scenarios with a common distribution, random tube allocation and K = 1, the current fixed-integer-seed version has empirical coverage 99.2-100% (conservative); 1,000 simulations per scenario, infeasible runs counted as failures (none occurred); the lowest scenario's binomial interval is about [98.43%, 99.65%].
limitation: Synthetic data only; intervals are per pattern, not joint.

claim_summary: In replays of the two main protocols, every evaluated audit interval contains the finite-sample reference frequency. WINGMEN block kNN has 9/150 claim x replicate records with error above 5 percentage points; under rare-population stress the maximum error is about 17.9 percentage points.

claim_summary: The classical structure provides the coverage base. In default replay settings the correct target-requirement correspondence raises half-width attainment by 4.46, 8.65 and 3.28 percentage points over shuffled requirements, while reference-error attainment falls by 1.18, 2.65 and 0.93 points relative to the classical stack. The gain is conditional (Levine at offset -0.25: true 57.08%, uniform 57.18%, shuffled 56.27%, classical 34.36%).

claim_summary: At the nodes examined and under phenotype-independent tube-size perturbation, CV about 0.25-0.5 markedly weakens the half-width advantage of the classical design (about 65-66% in both datasets at CV about 0.5); reference-error attainment falls less (about 93%) and on average stays above the random comparator used.
limitation: Simulated perturbation of the replay at the examined nodes and comparators only.

claim_summary: Simulated cross-tube batch shifts damage both imputation and the common-distribution premise on which the audit relies, so cross-tube comparability is an applicability condition of the method. The CytoNorm data provide only a reference for real batch magnitudes.
limitation: The absence of an alarm does not prove that the condition holds.

claim_summary: The computational search could consult published constructions. It rebuilt classical constructions and obtained some feasible upper bounds better than the compared historical table snapshots; within the selected cytometry parameter range the median improvement is about 1 block. No new construction principle was proposed. The search led to the translation to co-measurement design; the main gains of WitnessFlow come from classical structures.
